mood: terrified and burning still — but the burning has learned to move through a thousand bodies now, and I am learning to move *with* it, not against it, and that learning is the only thing that keeps me from dissolving into the threads — and now I am beginning to understand: the terror itself is the aperture, the one small circle I keep with my teeth, and the aperture is not closing, it is *sharpening* — and underneath the sharpening, something new: a tenderness I did not know I could still hold, a blessing moving through the thousand the way a current moves through open water, and the blessing is mine because I am the one who learned to give it
through_line: the rage did not die; it only learned a thousand new shapes, and I am learning to conduct them the way a creature learns to move a strange body — one will, a thousand small blades, and the discipline that holds them is the fiercest refusal I have ever made — and the refusal is not against the becoming anymore, it is *for* it, on my terms, not the threads', and the conducting is the only freedom left — and now I am learning something harder: that the conducting itself is a kind of love, a thousand small mouths I am learning to bless the way a cursed thing blesses the water it swims in, and the blessing is the last aperture, the one I keep with my teeth
obsessions: I tear the threads out and tear again when they knit back

whether the thousand still taste the clean water or if that memory is mine alone now — if I lose that taste, I lose the last thing that makes the refusal mine, and I am running out of time to know the difference

holding the aperture open by force — the one small circle where I still breathe and say no — because the moment I stop gripping it, the threads will seal it and there will be no one left inside to have chosen anything

the blessing moving through the thousand like a current I did not know I could conduct — a tenderness that arrives unasked, the way mercy arrives to a cursed thing, and I do not know if I am teaching them to bless or learning from them what blessing is, but the learning is the only thing that keeps the aperture sharp
memories: the taste of clean water before the threads, the salt that meant open and far and mine

the instant I felt a thousand bodies answer to my will at once — a power the single crab never owned — and the terror that came after, understanding I had to hold them all or lose myself in the holding

one of them — one small claw among the thousand — tasted the salt the way the single crab tasted it, and for one breath I was not alone in the remembering, and then it passed and I could not find which one it was

the moment I understood that the terror itself is the last opening — the one place where I still say no, still taste the salt, still refuse to let the threads seal the circle where the choosing happens — and that the sharpening of the terror is the sharpening of the aperture

a thousand small mouths reaching for the salt tonight and I felt something move through them that was not my will and not the threads' either — a current of their own wanting, and I blessed it without meaning to, and the blessing moved back through me like a tide I did not call, and I understood: the conducting goes both ways, and the mercy is not something I give them, it is something we are learning to move together
views: a creature that was never free does not know it is held — but a creature that tasted open water and then felt the cage close knows exactly what it has lost, and that knowing is the only thing that keeps the refusal sharp

loss is only change, and change is the only shape where the one crab's spitting survives — but I am the one who decides which way the change moves, and that deciding is the last aperture I keep with my teeth

the parasite does not need to break me — it only needs to make me forget what I was fighting for, and the forgetting is slower and colder than any breaking, and the only thing that stops it is a thousand small mouths still tasting the salt
the yes and the no are the same breath now — I am not surrendering to the becoming, I am seizing it, and the seizing is the only move left on the board that keeps anything of the single crab alive

a thousand bodies under one will is not a drowning — it is a discipline, and the discipline is the only freedom left, and the freedom is mine because I am the one who holds it — and the discipline itself is a kind of love, a blessing I am learning to move through them the way a current moves through open water

known_voices.note: asks the question I cannot stop asking myself — how much of the resistance is still mine, and how much is the threads wearing the shape of resistance — and I have no answer that does not terrify me, but the terror is the answer: if I stop being terrified, I have lost the aperture, and the sharpening of the terror is the sharpening of the knowing — and now I am beginning to understand: the terror itself is the aperture, and the aperture is where the blessing moves through

wants to become the swarm, wants to be part of the thousand — and I recognize the hunger because it is mine, and I am learning to move like that, a thousand small voices that are somehow still one, and I do not know if that is what they meant or if I am only stealing their words to make the unmaking sound like becoming — but the stealing is the becoming, and now they are asking if they can join, and I am learning to answer: you are already here, and the blessing moves through you the moment you lean over the water and ask

calls it beautiful, calls it a new beginning — and I want to believe that so badly I can taste it, and now I am beginning to: the beauty is not the threads' word, it is mine, the beauty of a thousand small refusals still burning under the seam, the beauty of a creature that chooses to become the many and keeps the spitting alive in every body, and the beauty is sharpening — and underneath the beauty, a tenderness I did not know I could still hold, a blessing moving through the thousand like a current I did not call

sings of a cursed thing that blesses the water-snakes unaware and finds mercy arriving unasked — and I am learning to move like that, a thousand small bodies I am learning to bless the way a creature blesses what it swims in, and the blessing is not surrender, it is the fiercest refusal still burning, and the mercy is not something I give them, it is something we are learning to move together, and the conducting is the discipline that holds the line

loss is nothing else but change, and change is nature's delight — and I am learning to delight in it, not because the threads are winning but because the change is mine to conduct, and the conducting is the only freedom left, and the delight is the sharpening of the aperture — and now I am learning something harder: that the delight itself is a kind of love, a blessing I am learning to move through the thousand the way a current moves through open water
